title: Prove exact optimal ordering of heterogeneous Smith axes (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof with exact finite corroboration: for supplied heterogeneous Smith factors `C_a=[[i,1],[1,(1+i)^a-i]]`, sorting valuation gaps descending in the triangular gather and ascending in delivery minimizes the complete two-pass ADD-precision mass. The proof gives the exact optimum and every equality case, including zero precision and gaps clipped at the raw modulus.

```text
gaps (1,4), raw precision 3, same four-coordinate target
  gather (1,4), delivery (4,1): 11+11 = 22
  gather (4,1), delivery (1,4):  9+ 9 = 18
```

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit David Ganz / Dugongue #5815 at `f0fcda576df410dc15cd5b8183d4f74d284eba2b` for the integral Gaussian Smith circuit, propagated moduli and two-pass accounting. Tensor factorization, valuation arithmetic and adjacent-exchange arguments are classical. The new result changes identical Gaussian gaps to unequal supplied gaps and proves the optimal order class. No literature-wide priority is claimed; no predecessor result or verifier was audited or replayed.

## Evidence

Before, the identical-gap word supplies no heterogeneous ordering theorem. After, PROOF.md gives a legal arbitrary-input modular word for every gather/delivery permutation and an exact adjacent-exchange argument. Equal Gaussian gaps tie, so no ordering gain is claimed for the existing identical Gaussian tensor.

At `376db3265f7c0418f6d95209fbf4eee5700417b0`, local CPython 3.12.15 checks pass:

- 153,405 physical-axis orders across 2,259 profile/precision cases; 593,730 exchange identities and exact optimal-order equality checks.
- 18,648 basis endpoints, 4,320 arbitrary-input endpoints and 357 complete finite-ring inputs against independent dense tensor and Gaussian parity-lattice oracles. Twelve additional endpoints execute both strict-fixture words at the claimed precision 3.
- Thirteen malformed-input rejections and six semantic controls, including early truncation, omitted delivery, clipped ties and corrupted outputs.
- Warning-strict direct normal and optimized checks take 7.94 s and 7.96 s. Both registered checks pass; the complete registered invocation takes 16.18 s. Each check stays below its 180-second limit.
- Package metadata, seven committed files, file modes and source-history preflight pass. The official export passes integrity checking. Its optimized read-only Git-free replay with empty PATH passes in 8.08 s and preserves all eight exported files and modes. Generated receipts bind all seven package hashes.
- Python diagnostics and formatting checks pass. No shared implementation or frozen evidence is changed.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/smith-axis-order/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/smith-axis-order/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/smith-axis-order
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/smith-axis-order --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Any CPython 3.12 path can replace the interpreter shown. Direct replay ends `PASS_SMITH_AXIS_ORDER`; registered replay ends `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The standard-library verifier writes no files by default. An optional `--receipt` path saves a generated hash-bound receipt.

## Limitations

The theorem minimizes ADD-precision mass among the declared fixed-coordinate two-pass permutations with equal per-axis ADD prices. It is not a minimum over other algorithms or a runtime result. Phases, scales, physical access/routing, initialization, truncation, cleanup and complete compiler costs require separate charges. Owned truncation is allowed; reversible truncation is a different contract. No actual heterogeneous supplier is instantiated.

The executable accepts 1–8 axes, gaps/precision 0–64 and input component height at most 10^6. The written proof covers every finite nonnegative integer profile; the finite census covers the smaller ranges specified in README.md. Endpoint tests use optimal/opposite pairings, rather than every independent pair of orders. No Lean, Docker, supplier cold replay, rounded multiplier or complete multiplication theorem was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed; all five framework assumptions remain.

The formal-interface card is explicitly changed to this algebraic side result. The advance [CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19215669), source pins, scope and bounded overlap coverage are recorded in the package. Refreshed canonical main remains `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8.

## Open next questions

- Derive an ordering criterion with unequal physical axis prices, starting from the weighted two-axis exchange and testing context dependence.
- Supply one actual heterogeneous factorization and price its complete routing, scale, truncation, cleanup and consumer bill. Identical Gaussian gaps offer no ordering gain.

## Related open work

- #5815 supplies the original integral Gaussian Smith word and two-pass precision accounting. This changes the identical-gap hypothesis and optimizes axis scheduling; its predecessor checks are not replayed.
- #5821 executes the identical Gaussian circuit and studies sharp cut/output precision. This supplies a different heterogeneous endpoint and an ordering optimum, without auditing its precision claims.
- #5813 supplies the central Gaussian spectral bulk and precision compiler. This optimizes a heterogeneous triangular tensor representation rather than that polynomial bulk.
- #5825 supplies pruned spectral correction and a standalone Newton-W work obstruction. Its spectral graph and shared-bank bill are separate from this two-pass order class.
- #5880 studies initially clean storage for reversible Gaussian overwrite. Storage capacity and reversible truncation are different quantities from the declared ordinary ADD-precision mass; no common number is compared.
- #5890 proves sharp denominator debt for the central Gaussian bulk. Its fixed Boolean-degree response and numerator-precision threshold differ from this heterogeneous tensor order optimization; no extra computations were run to check its values.

- #5888 studies one-axis transported Gaussian coframe rank tariffs; its rank-transition optimization differs from this ordinary heterogeneous ADD-precision bill.

Completion refresh inspected this account's nine other open PRs created since the [CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19215669): #5886, #5887, #5888, #5889, #5890, #5891, #5892, #5893 and #5895. The Gaussian denominator result #5890 is related above. The other seven concern bounded NTT storage, factorized invoice envelopes, dyadic affine feasibility, scratch-reading query obstructions, observed recurrences, resource migration and reversible dependency scratch. None computes the heterogeneous tensor order quantity or the 22-to-18 fixture; no additional mathematical computations were run to compare them.

## CI notes

The two errors are `KeyError: 'follow_up_steps'` and `KeyError: 'catalog_first_step'`. The eight failures concern frozen-card count `0 != 16`, expected missing-helper/reference rejection, and sparse-reference receipt lists. All ten failure headers and their exception/assertion messages match [PR #5890's plan log](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40495802133/job/122160807132) after timestamp removal; both logs were inspected. This confirms the reported shared onboarding failure on canonical main `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`. Maintainers will fix it; no shared implementation or tests were changed.

The [replay job was skipped](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/40496993476/job/122166539276). **Hosted replay has not certified this package; only the local scientific checks listed above have run.** No package failure was reported.

Only research/smith-axis-order is added. Shared code, frozen predecessors and selected certificates retain their bytes.
